answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake to a shared registry before it can submit work, and the protocol caps how much influence any one stake can buy. When an agent’s claim is challenged, randomly selected peers verify its work; a proven duplicate identity loses its stake, which is split among challengers. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it, rather than creating accounts for free. A juniper, walnut, or vertex label changes nothing; only bonded, verified participation earns influence.
